body: - **Step 7a.1 — 9 explicit plan-listed path(s) untouched by the working-tree delta before dispatcher commit. First 10**: python/tests/design/test_plan_quality.py, python/tests/calibration/test_difficulty.py, python/tests/implement/test_preflight.py, python/tests/agents/test_agents.py, python/tests/design/test_design_lifecycle.py, python/tests/design/test_design_publish.py, python/tests/state/test_bootstrap.py, python/tests/issue/test_issue_wire.py, python/tests/review/test_plan_review.py

- lint-fix tier=claude category=authentication-preflight; Verification complete. Both signals the checks harness uses now pass on the edited file:
- **pyright CLI: `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations`** (was the sole failure — `reportUnusedFunction` on `_is_trailer_region_line:118`)
- **ruff CLI: `All checks passed!`**

The `<new-diagnostics>` note about `_capture_design_transcript` is a spurious editor-LSP artifact from the line-number shift (692→683 after removing 9 lines): that function already carried its `# pyright: ignore[reportUnusedFunction]` before my edit and is genuinely called cross-module at `design_log_publish_flow.py:725`. The CLI pyright — the one the harness runs — confirms 0 errors. I did not touch the unrelated `preflight.py` working-tree change.

The fix removed dead code that this branch's own round-2 refactor orphaned: `_splice_plan_provenance` was rewritten to use `plan_grammar.parse_final_trailers`, deleting both call sites of `_is_trailer_region_line`, and `_PROVENANCE_META_KEYS` existed only to serve that function.

FIXED: python/larch/design/design_publish.py | pyright reportUnusedFunction on `_is_trailer_region_line` (dead code orphaned by the plan-grammar refactor); removed it and its now-orphaned `_PROVENANCE_META_KEYS` constant

- One G-Cfg-3 deviation: `_RECOGNIZED_TRAILER_PREFIX_RE` in `python/larch/implement/preflight.py` (added in this diff at line ~962) manually re-lists all eight trailer key names (`review_status|rounds_completed|difficulty|diff_added|diff_deleted|mechanical_churn|oversize_override|diff_lines`) as a string literal instead of deriving from `plan_grammar.TRAILER_KEYS`. This is the same convention whose canonical definition was just centralized in plan_grammar.py. If a new trailer key is added to `plan_grammar.TRAILER_KEYS`, this regex silently fails to flag malformed trailer lines for that key during preflight. The fix is `re.compile(r'^(' + '|'.join(plan_grammar.TRAILER_KEYS) + r'):')`. All other consumers correctly delegate to plan_grammar, and the fence-aware heading parsing (G-Md-3), consumer sweep (G-Wire-1, G-Wire-3), and frozen-dataclass use (G-Py-1) are compliant.
